title: Identity, composition and structure-unit equations for tensor-section coordinates
statement: For schemes [def-pc-scheme] let $P_a=a^*$ be tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], $c_{a,b}:P_aP_b\simeq P_{ba}$ its unit-normalized composition comparison, $i_X:P_{\mathrm{id}_X}\simeq\mathrm{id}$ the normalized identity comparison, and $e_a:P_a\mathcal O\simeq\mathcal O$ the adjoint structure-module comparison. Write $\rho_F$ for the normalized tensor-section restriction [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]. They satisfy three equations. (1) For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $t:W\to X$ in the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $\Gamma(P_t i_X)\Gamma(c_{t,\mathrm{id}_X,F}^{-1})=\rho_F(k_{\mathrm{id}})$, where $k_{\mathrm{id}}:t\to\mathrm{id}_X\circ t$ is the canonical site arrow with underlying scheme map $\mathrm{id}_W$. (2) For etale $v:Y\to X$, $w:Z\to Y$, $t:W\to Z$ and arbitrary $F$ on $X$, $\Gamma(P_t c_{w,v,F})\Gamma(c_{t,w,P_vF}^{-1})\Gamma(c_{wt,v,F}^{-1})=\Gamma(c_{t,vw,F}^{-1})\rho_F(k_{\mathrm{assoc}})$, where $k_{\mathrm{assoc}}:(vw)t\to v(wt)$ is the canonical site arrow, again with underlying scheme map $\mathrm{id}_W$. (3) For etale $v:Y\to X$ and $t:W\to Y$, $\Gamma(e_t)\Gamma(P_t e_v)\Gamma(c_{t,v,\mathcal O_X}^{-1})=\Gamma(e_{vt})$. The isomorphisms here are exactly the library's $\texttt{tensorSectionsComp}$, $\texttt{trfTensorId}$ and $\texttt{trfTensorUnit}$. Neither quasi-coherence nor invertibility of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Instantiate lem-trf-section-adjunction-coordinate-coherence with the recorded tensor-pullback adjunctions. Its identity-section equation evaluates restriction along the canonical identity site arrow; its right-unit cancellation equation gives the desired inverse comparison formula. These are the actual normalized tensor comparisons by their definitions.

Use the inverse-associativity equation of lem-trf-section-adjunction-coordinate-coherence on W -> Z -> Y -> X and take global sections. Its identity-section equation evaluates the canonical associativity site arrow, whose underlying scheme map is the identity. The result is exactly the required equation, with its specified parenthesizations.

The hom of trfTensorUnit agrees with the adjoint structure-sheaf map by the unit equation for leftAdjointUniq. Apply the composite adjunction Hom equivalence to c followed by the composite structure-sheaf map and to the composite of the pulled-back structure-sheaf maps. The unit equation for c and naturality move both to the composite structure-ring map. Injectivity identifies them. Cancel c and take sections, proving (3).

theorem trf_tensor_sections_coordinate_coherence :
    (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (F : X.Modules) (W : X.Etale)
      (s : Γ((Modules.tensorPullback (W.hom ≫ 𝟙 X)).obj F, ⊤)),
      ((Modules.tensorPullback W.hom).map ((trfTensorId X).hom.app F)).app ⊤
        (((Modules.tensorSectionsComp W.hom (𝟙 X)).inv.app F).app ⊤ s) =
      Modules.etaleTensorSectionsRestriction F (trfEtaleIdArrow W) s) ∧
    (∀ (X Y Z : Scheme.{u}) (v : Y ⟶ X) (w : Z ⟶ Y) [Etale v] [Etale w]
      (F : X.Modules) (W : Z.Etale)
      (s : Γ((Modules.tensorPullback ((W.hom ≫ w) ≫ v)).obj F, ⊤)),
      ((Modules.tensorPullback W.hom).map
        ((Modules.tensorSectionsComp w v).hom.app F)).app ⊤
          (((Modules.tensorSectionsComp W.hom w).inv.app
            ((Modules.tensorPullback v).obj F)).app ⊤
              (((Modules.tensorSectionsComp (W.hom ≫ w) v).inv.app F).app ⊤ s)) =
      ((Modules.tensorSectionsComp W.hom (w ≫ v)).inv.app F).app ⊤
        (Modules.etaleTensorSectionsRestriction F (trfEtaleCompArrow v w W) s)) ∧
    (∀ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (v : Y ⟶ X) [Etale v] (W : Y.Etale)
      (s : Γ((Modules.tensorPullback (W.hom ≫ v)).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf), ⊤)),
      (trfTensorUnit W.hom).hom.app ⊤
        (((Modules.tensorPullback W.hom).map (trfTensorUnit v).hom).app ⊤
          (((Modules.tensorSectionsComp W.hom v).inv.app
            (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).app ⊤ s)) =
      (trfTensorUnit (W.hom ≫ v)).hom.app ⊤ s)
